info.name: SmartFoodOps API
info.description:
Every route the Nginx gateway exposes across all 7 services (user, restaurant, menu, order, payment, rider, orchestrator), organised and asserted the same way scripts/smoke-test.sh drives them: happy path, authorisation boundaries, edge cases, and the Temporal-driven order saga end to end.

**Run order matters.** Folders 1-9 are numbered because later ones depend on variables (tokens, ids) captured by earlier ones. Run the whole collection with the Collection Runner, top to bottom, in one sitting -- individual folders can be re-run later, but only after folder 2 has populated tokens in this session.

**Folders 7 and 8 contain self-looping poll requests** (they re-send themselves via `postman.setNextRequest` until the order reaches the status they're waiting on, up to a bounded number of tries) -- since Week 2 the order lifecycle is driven by a Temporal saga, so a status is reached *eventually*, not by the time the request that triggered it returns. These only work in the Collection Runner, not on a single Send click; set a ~2000ms delay between requests there.

**Two things smoke-test.sh checks that this collection can't**: it reads three tables directly (payments, order_tracking_logs, riders) via `docker exec` to assert refunds, trail rows and fleet-leak invariants no HTTP response exposes, and it drives two compensation paths (no rider available, kitchen at capacity) that need direct database manipulation to set up. Both are read-only observations layered on top of the same HTTP contract this collection already exercises.

See readme/observability-and-eventing-guide.md and readme/order-saga-orchestration-guide.md for how the pieces underneath these routes actually work.

item.name: 7. Order Saga -- Happy Path to 'delivered'

request.description: Self-looping poll (Collection Runner only -- set a ~2000ms delay in the Runner so this doesn't hammer the gateway). Re-sends itself up to 30 times until the order reaches 'confirmed', mirroring smoke-test.sh's poll_status(). Runs after checkout; the saga authorises payment and confirms before the kitchen can act on it.

exec: try { rbody = pm.response.json().body; status = rbody.status; } catch (e) {}

request.description: The kitchen projection is deliberately narrower than the full order -- moving the queue onto `orders` must not widen what a restaurant can see about a customer's order.

exec: pm.test("envelope status matches HTTP status", () => { const j = pm.response.json(); if (j && typeof j.status !== "undefined") pm.expect(String(j.status)).to.eql(String(pm.response.code)); });
